findings.title: OaK: Ontology-as-a-Kernel for Dynamic LLM Agent Behavior
findings.key_findings: Introduces OaK (Ontology-as-a-Kernel), a framework that dynamically constructs and refines task-oriented ontologies for LLM agents. OaK packages the task interface into a kernel K=(S,F) where S is a task-oriented schema defining domain concepts, properties, and relations, and F defines typed reasoning functions (retrieval, filtering, traversal, projection, aggregation, multi-step reasoning). The framework constructs a schema-guided knowledge graph G from task data and uses judge-driven refinement with official task scores and execution trajectories to iteratively repair schema and functions before freezing for inference. Evaluated on TravelPlanner, CRMArenaPro, and ToolQA showing consistent gains across backbones.

findings.title: DIAL-KG: Schema-Free Incremental Knowledge Graph Construction via Dynamic Schema Induction and Evolution-Intent Assessment
findings.key_findings: Proposes DIAL-KG, a closed-loop framework for incremental KG construction anchored by a Meta-Knowledge Base (MKB). Operates in a three-stage cycle: (1) Dual-Track Extraction (defaults to triple generation, switches to event extraction for complex knowledge), (2) Governance Adjudication (evidence verification, consistency checks, intent recognition, auditable soft deprecation as transactional updates), (3) Schema Evolution (new schemas induced from validated knowledge to guide subsequent construction cycles). Achieves SOTA performance in extraction quality and induced schema quality, with 4.7% F1 improvement over baselines, >98% precision on soft deprecations, and 15% fewer relation types with reduced redundancy.

findings.title: Evo-DKD: Dual-Knowledge Decoding for Autonomous Ontology Evolution in Large Language Models
findings.key_findings: Introduces Evo-DKD, a dual-decoder framework for autonomous ontology evolution combining structured ontology traversal with unstructured text reasoning. Two parallel decoding streams: structured decoder generates ontology edits (class insertions, relation assertions, schema modifications in OWL/RDF), unstructured decoder produces natural language explanations. Dynamic attention-based gating mechanism coordinates streams, deciding at each step how to blend structured and unstructured knowledge. Validation module checks proposed edits using both KB constraints and generated text for factual plausibility. Closed-loop autonomous updating feeds ontology updates back into LLM context for subsequent iterations. Outperforms single-modality baselines on triple extraction accuracy, explanation quality (BLEU, BERTScore), and output reliability across healthcare, semantic search, and cultural heritage domains.

findings.title: DySECT: Dynamic Self-Evolving Extraction and Curation Toolkit
findings.key_findings: Proposes DySECT, a dynamic self-evolving extraction system that continually improves as used. Forms a closed-loop: LLM extraction populates a self-expanding KB with triples; KB enriches itself through probabilistic confidence modeling and graph-based reasoning (hierarchical clustering for concept abstraction, mutual-exclusivity constraints); enriched KB feeds back into extractor via prompt tuning, few-shot sampling, or KB-derived synthetic data for fine-tuning. Uses conservative noisy-or aggregation with shrinkage factor for confidence scoring, penalizing mutual-exclusivity conflicts. Code available at github.com/megagonlabs/dysect. Simulates self-evolving loop in three stages on DocRED.

findings.title: DSE-RE: Dynamic Schema Evolution with LLM for Iterative Relation Extraction
findings.key_findings: Proposes DSE-RE, a closed-loop feedback system for dynamic schema evolution in relation extraction. Three components: (1) LLM-Driven Inference (LLM-DI) for entity-relation identification, (2) Evolving Schema Registry (ESR) that dynamically constructs/optimizes entity type tables and relation type tables embedded as contextual guidance in prompts, (3) Graph-Based Semantic Clustering Algorithm (GSCA) to merge synonymous redundancies and control schema expansion. Evaluated on FOBIE benchmark (+3% F1) and Huizhou-style Architecture dataset (+6.8% F1). Demonstrates improved adaptability in low-resource scenarios over supervised models.

findings.title: EOAC-LLM: An LLM-driven Event Ontology Automatic Construction System
findings.key_findings: Presents EOAC-LLM, a fully automated, LLM-driven event ontology construction framework with five core modules: event ontology modeling corpus generation, event element-relation extraction, deep semantic representation and aggregation, event ontology generation, and dynamic update. Key novelties: (1) full-process automation eliminating manual annotation/expert knowledge, (2) semantic-temporal-relation multi-space fusion model with dynamic weighting for accurate semantic mapping, (3) temporal relation-aware hierarchical clustering algorithm addressing uneven event cluster granularity via temporal consistency scoring, (4) event gap identification and incremental update mechanism enabling self-driven dynamic evolution. Validated in emergency disaster relief with DeepSeek, Doubao, ERNIE Bot — outperforms baselines by >15% F1 in event extraction.

findings.title: OntoRipple: Automated Propagation of Ontology Changes to RML Mappings and SHACL Shapes
findings.key_findings: Presents OntoRipple, a tool automating propagation of ontology changes into RML mappings and SHACL shapes for KG construction/validation. Supports 25 distinct change operations from the OWL Change Ontology covering OWL classes, properties, class/property relations, and property characteristics. Change Propagation Engine processes changes in predefined order (e.g., AddClass before AddSubClass for same class). When assumptions are made about propagation, modified triples are added to review mappings for user verification. Demonstrated on Public Procurement Data Space / eProcurement Ontology (versions 3.0.0 to 3.0.1). Available at github.com/oeg-upm/OntoRipple.

findings.title: ATOM: AdapTive and OptiMized Dynamic Temporal Knowledge Graph Construction using LLMs
findings.key_findings: Proposes ATOM, a few-shot scalable approach for building/updating Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGs) from unstructured text. Key innovations: (1) Atomic fact decomposition — splits documents into minimal self-contained 'atomic' facts for exhaustive/stable extraction, (2) Dual-time modeling — distinguishes observation time (when fact observed) from validity period (when fact true in world), (3) Parallel 5-tuple extraction and parallel atomic TKG merging for scalability. Achieves ~18% higher exhaustivity, ~17% better stability, and >90% latency reduction vs baselines. Dual-time modeling enables proper inference of relative times and TKG dynamism.

findings.title: AutoSchemaKG: Autonomous Knowledge Graph Construction through Dynamic Schema Induction from Web-Scale Corpora
findings.key_findings: Presents AutoSchemaKG, a fully autonomous KG construction framework eliminating predefined schemas. Two-stage approach: (1) KG triple extraction using LLMs for entities and events, (2) Schema induction via conceptualization — generates abstract conceptual categories for each entity/event/relation, organizes instances into semantic categories forming multi-level hierarchy. Creates ATLAS KG family (900M+ nodes, 5.9B edges). Achieves 92% semantic alignment with human-crafted schemas with zero manual intervention. Outperforms baselines on multi-hop QA and enhances LLM factuality.

findings.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory / Graphiti
findings.key_findings: Zep/Graphiti provides a temporal knowledge graph architecture for agent memory with bi-temporal modeling (valid time + ingestion/provenance time). Every edge carries timestamps: when fact became valid, when superseded, when learned, when learned false. Superseded facts are invalidated not deleted, preserving history. Graphiti is open-source temporal context graph engine (30K+ GitHub stars); Zep is managed platform with Context Graph Engine for millions of graphs at sub-200ms p95 retrieval. Hybrid retrieval combines vector, full-text, and graph traversal. Enables point-in-time queries: 'what was true then' vs 'what is true now'. LOCOMO benchmark: 94.7% accuracy, 155ms latency.

findings.title: Time is Not a Label: Continuous Phase Rotation for Temporal Knowledge Graphs and Agentic Memory
findings.key_findings: Introduces RoMem framework for temporal reasoning over agentic memory using continuous phase rotation. Addresses the challenge that graph-based memory systems (Mem0, HippoRAG, Zep, Graphiti, LicoMemory, DescGraph) model time as discrete labels, losing continuous temporal dynamics. Proposes continuous phase rotation to capture temporal evolution in embedding space. Evaluated on FinTMMBench for zero-shot generalization in high-volatility financial contexts, achieving 0.728 MRR and 0.580 LLM@5 accuracy under GPT-5-mini, outperforming A-Mem (0.716 MRR) and HippoRAG (0.690 MRR).

findings.title: Graph-based Agent Memory: Taxonomy, Techniques, and Applications
findings.key_findings: Comprehensive survey/taxonomy of graph-based agent memory systems. Categorizes memory into episodic (timestamped event nodes), semantic (domain facts as persistent KG), and procedural (tool-use patterns as workflow subgraphs). Analyzes extraction approaches (LLM-based, rule-based, hybrid), storage (property graphs in Neo4j/FalkorDB), retrieval (multi-hop, temporal, hybrid vector-graph), and evolution (incremental updates, entity resolution, schema evolution). Provides design patterns for four-phase lifecycle: extraction, storage, retrieval, evolution. References Zep/Graphiti, Mem0, Neo4j Agent Memory, FalkorDB as key implementations.

findings.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with EvoReasoner and EvoKG
findings.key_findings: Presents unified framework for temporal reasoning over evolving KGs combining EvoReasoner (multi-hop temporal reasoning with multi-route decomposition, global-local entity grounding, temporally grounded scoring) and EvoKG (noise-tolerant KG evolution module that incrementally updates KG from unstructured documents through confidence-based contradiction resolution). Unlike static retrieval augmentation, tightly couples temporal reasoning with dynamic KG construction/updating. Addresses contradiction resolution and temporal trend modeling jointly for accurate reasoning in dynamic knowledge environments.

findings.title: KnoBuilder: An LLM-Agent for Autonomous and Personalized Knowledge Graph Construction
findings.key_findings: Introduces KnoBuilder, an LLM-agent framework for autonomous KG construction from unstructured text. Implements synergistic loop between LLM agent and dynamically evolving KG. Features: strategic planning for knowledge acquisition, self-refining extraction with multi-stage validation, dynamic consolidation maintaining graph coherence. Achieves 85% F1 extraction quality, 46% improvement in acquisition efficiency, 91% entity resolution accuracy, 96% graph consistency scores on scientific corpora.

findings.title: iText2KG: Incremental Knowledge Graphs Construction Using Large Language Models
findings.key_findings: Incremental zero-shot KG construction method resolving semantic ambiguity via user-defined blueprints. Core limitation: inability to proactively discover knowledge types beyond blueprint scope and lack of mechanisms for dynamic knowledge evolution (revising/deprecating outdated knowledge). Serves as baseline for DIAL-KG and ATOM improvements.

findings.title: Multi-source Knowledge Graph Construction through LLM-assisted Incremental Fusion
findings.key_findings: Proposes multi-agent incremental fusion pipeline for multi-source KG construction handling structured (MySQL), semi-structured (JSON), and unstructured text. Core innovation: dual-support conflict detection combining rule-based text similarity with structure-based graph topology, followed by LLM-assisted resolution. Entity-level early fusion achieves 18.9% improvement in context recall (0.876 vs 0.737) and 64.6% improvement in multi-hop reasoning context recall (0.874 vs 0.531) vs query-time fusion.

findings.title: Active Ontology: The 2026 Default for Enterprise AI (Atlan)
findings.key_findings: Defines 'Active Ontology' as ontology bound to live metadata, lineage, and policy — definitions update as data estate evolves. Contrasts with static ontologies that drift by day 30. Four co-located graphs: data, governance, knowledge, active ontology sharing a metadata lakehouse substrate. Agents query active ontology via MCP at inference time. Includes drift detection via operational signals feeding governance graph with explicit drift dashboards. Versioning and auditability for definitions built-in.

findings.title: Ontology Drift: Why Your Knowledge Graph Is Slowly Going Wrong
findings.key_findings: Analyzes ontology drift as silent killer of enterprise KG projects. 27% of organizations have KGs in production (late 2025), flat from 26% prior year despite Graph RAG advances. Identifies drift causes: semantic drift (LLM outputs semantically equivalent but different expressions), schema rigidity, lack of automated validation. Proposes adversarial negative competency questions (AnIML ontology 2026) — questions ontology should NOT answer incorrectly, mapped to anti-patterns enforced via SHACL. Recommends versioned schema, review cycles, competency question updates as maintenance practice.

summary: As of September 2026, dynamic ontology research has converged on several key paradigms: (1) Ontology-as-a-Kernel (OaK) treats ontology as an executable interface coupling schema with typed reasoning functions, enabling task-conditioned construction and judge-driven refinement. (2) Closed-loop incremental KG construction (DIAL-KG, KnoBuilder, iText2KG) uses Meta-Knowledge Bases and dual-track extraction with governance adjudication for auditable, transactional updates without full reconstruction. (3) Dual-knowledge decoding (Evo-DKD) employs parallel structured/unstructured decoders with dynamic gating for autonomous ontology evolution, validated via cross-verification. (4) Dynamic self-evolving extraction (DySECT) creates symbiotic loops where extraction populates a probabilistic KB that feeds back via prompts/fine-tuning. (5) Schema evolution (DSE-RE, AutoSchemaKG, EOAC-LLM) uses LLMs to dynamically induce/optimize schemas with graph-based clustering for redundancy control, achieving 92% alignment with human schemas. (6) Ontology change propagation (OntoRipple) automates 25 OWL change operations to RML/SHACL artifacts in declarative workflows. (7) Temporal KGs (ATOM, Zep/Graphiti, RoMem) adopt dual-time modeling (observation vs validity) and bi-temporal edges for point-in-time queries, with >90% latency reduction. (8) Versioned memory graphs (Zep/Graphiti, Mem0g) implement git-style versioning with validity windows on all edges, enabling temporal reasoning and drift detection. The field is shifting from static construction to continuous, governed evolution with embedded provenance and automated drift management.
